MISP contains an authorization bypass in its event search and filter functionality. When a user performed searches through events/restSearch (value, value prefix, searchall, type, uuid, attribute tags, object filters), objects/restSearch, or the event index tag, galaxy, and quick filters, the underlying SQL subqueries matched against attributes and objects without enforcing the per-attribute distribution, sharing-group, or soft-deleted visibility rules that apply when fetching individual elements.

A user who could view an event (for example, a community-distributed event) could therefore use search to determine whether organisation-only, sharing-group-restricted, or soft-deleted attributes and objects existed within that event. Because the value filter supports prefix matching (LIKE), an attacker could enumerate the full value of a hidden attribute one character at a time. Tags attached exclusively to hidden attributes also leaked through the tag, galaxy, and quick-filter paths on the event index.

The vulnerability affects the EventsController quick-filter and index-filter logic, the Event model wildcard/value/uuid/tag filter methods, the MispAttribute tag filter, the MispObject buildFilterConditions and restSearch methods, and the ReportFromEvent object filter. Site administrators and users belonging to the event's own organisation retain full visibility, and sync users continue to match soft-deleted elements as intended.

The issue was reported by ENISA.

MISP contains an authorization bypass in the correlations/eventCorrelations endpoint and the underlying correlation engines (Default and OnDemand). The CorrelationsController::eventCorrelations action did not verify that the requesting user was permitted to view the event specified by the event ID parameter. Any authenticated user could supply the ID of an event belonging to another organisation (distribution level 0, organisation-only) and receive its full correlation results, including attribute identifiers and values. Additionally, for events the user could partially view, the correlation engines filtered only the related (target) side of each correlation row and did not vet the queried event's own source attributes. As a result, correlations keyed by attributes hidden from the user (organisation-only attributes, attributes in sharing groups the user is not a member of, or attributes inside organisation-only objects) were returned with their IDs and values. The Default engine's related-event listing (used in events/view) also included events related solely through such hidden attributes. The vulnerability was reported by ENISA. Successful exploitation requires a valid authenticated session with any role and knowledge or enumeration of a target event ID. The security impact is disclosure of threat-intelligence attribute values (IP addresses, domain names, etc.) and attribute identifiers that the user is not authorised to see, as well as confirmation of the existence of otherwise invisible events.

MISP's EventDelegationsController delegateEvent method accepted a user-supplied sharing_group_id parameter without verifying that the requesting user was a member of the referenced sharing group. When a delegation request was submitted with distribution set to 4 (sharing-group distribution), the raw sharing_group_id value was stored directly into the EventDelegation record. The delegation view subsequently rendered the stored sharing group's name back to the requester. Because no authorization check was performed, any authenticated user with delegation permission could enumerate sharing group identifiers (by guessing sequential IDs or other values) and read the names of sharing groups to which their organisation did not belong, including hidden or restricted groups. Hidden, missing, and malformed identifiers were not distinguished in the response, but the successful case still leaked the group name. The vulnerability required an authenticated session with the perm_delegate capability and knowledge of a valid event ID to delegate. The security impact is limited to disclosure of sharing group names (a low-impact confidentiality breach) and does not grant access to the group's contents or modify any data.

MISP contains an access control flaw in its tag management endpoints: events/addTag (single and bulk), events/removeTag, and attributes/removeTag. These endpoints loaded their target event or attribute using an unscoped database query (recursive = -1) that did not apply the calling user's ACL visibility rules. As a result, two distinct security issues existed: (1) Information disclosure: the removeTag endpoint returned different responses depending on whether a given tag was present on a hidden event, allowing an authenticated user to enumerate which tags were applied to events they had no visibility into. (2) Unauthorized modification: users belonging to the host organisation, who are permitted to set local tags on records they can see, could add or remove local tags on events and attributes they could not see, because the canModifyTag ACL check operated on the unscoped object without first verifying the caller's visibility. The fix replaces the unscoped find() calls with ACL-aware fetch methods (fetchSimpleEvent and fetchAttributeSimple) that apply the user's visibility before the object is returned, and adds an explicit empty-object check in removeTag so that a hidden event responds identically to a non-existent one. Affected components include the EventsController (addTag, removeTag), the AttributesController (removeTag), and the ACLComponent (canModifyTag). The vulnerability requires an authenticated user with at least the tagger role (perm_tagger) or host-organisation membership.

MISP contains an information disclosure vulnerability in the Sighting model when the Sightings_anonymise setting is enabled. The listSightings and sightings/restSearch endpoints accepted a caller-supplied org_id filter parameter and applied it directly to the SQL query without verifying whether the requesting user was authorized to filter by that organisation. Because the anonymization mechanism masks the reporter's organisation in the returned records, a non-site-admin user could bypass the anonymization by specifying another organisation's ID in the filter. The query would then return only that organisation's sightings, effectively naming the reporter and defeating the purpose of the anonymization feature. A negated filter (NOT IN) similarly revealed which sightings belonged to the target organisation by exclusion. The vulnerability requires an authenticated user with sighting read permissions (perm_sighting) who is not a site administrator, and the Sightings_anonymise plugin setting must be enabled. The security impact is the disclosure of which organisation reported a given sighting, undermining the privacy guarantees that the anonymization feature is designed to provide. This issue was reported by ENISA.

MISP contains an authorization flaw in the GalaxyCluster model's captureCluster() function, which handles the import and synchronization of Galaxy Clusters. Prior to the fix, any authenticated user holding the galaxy editor role could replace an existing locked Galaxy Cluster by supplying its UUID in an import request, regardless of which organization owned the cluster. The function unconditionally called captureOrganisationAndSG() before the save operation, overwriting the cluster's org_id and orgc_id fields with the importing user's organization, effectively transferring ownership of the cluster to the attacker's organization. Additionally, the save operation was not restricted to a specific set of fields, allowing arbitrary field modification.

The vulnerable behavior required the attacker to possess a valid MISP account with the perm_galaxy_editor role and to know or discover the UUID of a target cluster belonging to another organization. No site-admin or owner-organization privilege was enforced for the update path. The result was that a low-privilege galaxy editor in one organization could modify the content (value, description, distribution, etc.) of clusters owned by other organizations and seize ownership, corrupting the integrity of shared threat-intelligence data across the MISP instance.

The vulnerability was reported by ENISA and CERT.pl. The fix introduces an explicit authorization gate that restricts cluster updates to the owner organization, a sync user who can see the cluster via sharing-group rules, or a site administrator, and enforces a field allow-list that excludes org_id and orgc_id from update writes, preserving original ownership.

MISP contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the Galaxy import/sync functionality (captureGalaxy in app/Model/Galaxy.php). The captureGalaxy() method matched an incoming galaxy payload to an existing galaxy by UUID and unconditionally overwrote the matched record, regardless of whether the importing user belonged to the owning organization or whether the galaxy was a system-provided default galaxy. Any authenticated user holding the perm_galaxy_editor role could therefore: (1) demote a default galaxy by setting its default flag to false, (2) reassign the galaxy's org_id and orgc_id to the attacker's organization, effectively taking ownership, and (3) modify other galaxy fields (name, description, distribution, version). Additionally, the role-level permission check (perm_site_admin or perm_galaxy_editor) was executed after the captureOrganisationAndSG() call, meaning organization and sharing-group data was already captured before the authorization decision was made. The vulnerability requires an authenticated user with the perm_galaxy_editor role and the ability to submit a galaxy import payload containing a UUID that matches an existing galaxy. The security impact is loss of data integrity across the MISP instance: default galaxy definitions are corrupted, cross-organization ownership is silently transferred, and the integrity of shared threat-intelligence galaxy metadata is compromised for all users of the instance.

Meilisearch before 1.55.1 and 1.56.x before 1.56.1 contains a quadratic memory consumption vulnerability in filter-parser that allows attackers with a search API key to exhaust server memory. Attackers can send a roughly 100 KB filter, such as a _geoPolygon with thousands of coordinates, to the search endpoint, crashing the server and taking all indexes offline.

yt through 4.4.4 contains a code injection vulnerability that allows attackers to execute Python code by supplying a crafted con_args attribute in a ytdata HDF5 file. SavedDataset._parse_parameter_file() passes con_args to eval() unrestricted, so loading a malicious .h5 file with yt.load() runs attacker code as the user.

ScreenTinker before 3.2.4 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the GET /api/kiosk/:id/render endpoint that allows users with kiosk page edit rights to store javascript: URLs in page buttons. Attackers can trigger script execution in the dashboard origin when an administrator activates the button, hijacking the victim's session and taking full control of the instance.

MediaInfoLib before 26.10 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in File_Mpeg4::meta_iloc that allows attackers to trigger a global buffer over-read via oversized iloc field sizes. Attackers can supply a crafted MP4 file with invalid offset_size or length_size values to overrun the BitStream_Fast mask table and crash applications analysing the file.

MediaInfoLib before 26.10 contains a heap-based buffer over-read vulnerability in tfsxml_leave() caused by an off-by-one error when handling generic <! markup in truncated XML. Attackers can supply a crafted media file with malformed ADM XML parsed by File_Adm.cpp to crash MediaInfo or applications using MediaInfoLib.

Geany through 2.1.0 contains an OS command injection vulnerability that allows attackers to run shell commands by embedding metacharacters in filenames substituted into build and execute commands. Attackers can craft a file named with backticks or $(...) that executes via /bin/sh when a user runs Compile, Build or Execute, gaining code execution as the user.

GPAC MP4Box before 26.07.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in xmt_node_end() that allows attackers to crash the application through an unmatched closing ProtoDeclare element. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT-A scene file with a mismatched closing ProtoDeclare or ExternProtoDeclare element, causing a dereference of a NULL parsing_proto pointer and denial of service.

GPAC MP4Box before 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability because gf_node_free() frees nodes without detaching routes that still reference them via FromNode. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene with nested PROTO graphs so gf_sg_route_del() accesses freed memory, crashing MP4Box and potentially corrupting the heap.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in gf_isom_get_meta() in src/isomedia/meta.c that reads file->moov->trackList without checking the moov box exists. Attackers can supply a crafted ISOBMFF file with malformed AV1 configuration data that leaves moov unset, crashing MP4Box -infon and causing denial of service.

GPAC MP4Box before 26.07.0 contains a divide by zero vulnerability in DumpTrackInfo() in applications/mp4box/filedump.c that fails to check the media timescale for zero. Attackers can supply a crafted MP4 file with a zero media timescale to make MP4Box -infon raise SIGFPE and crash, causing denial of service.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains an integer underflow vulnerability in gf_xml_sax_peek_node() that allows attackers to write a zero byte outside the heap line buffer via crafted XML attribute values. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT file with a ROUTE or command referencing an undefined node, imported with MP4Box, to crash the process and corrupt memory.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in the XMT loader that leaves ROUTE commands of a discarded node queued after being freed by gf_sg_command_del(). Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene file imported with MP4Box so xmt_resolve_routes() writes to freed memory, corrupting the heap and crashing the process.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in MP4Box because gf_sg_reset frees DEF'd proto sub-graph nodes without removing them from the GF_Proto node_code list. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene with nested PROTOs so gf_sg_proto_del unregisters freed nodes during teardown, crashing MP4Box and corrupting the heap.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in xmt_parse_command() in loader_xmt.c that allows attackers to crash MP4Box via unchecked field lookups. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene whose atIndexField names a non-existent node field, causing a NULL read during import and denial of service.

GPAC MP4Box before 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in xmt_find_node() in loader_xmt.c that leaves freed forward-referenced nodes cached in parser->peeked_nodes. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT file with a node targeted by an SFCommandBuffer command, triggering a later DEF lookup on the freed node and crashing MP4Box.

GPAC MP4Box before 26.07.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in xmt_parse_proto() in loader_xmt.c that allows attackers to crash the process via a redefined ProtoDeclare name. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT file with a duplicate ProtoDeclare name, causing gf_sg_proto_new() to return NULL and crashing MP4Box during import.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in ReplaceDEFNode that allows attackers to crash MP4Box by triggering access to a partly freed child list. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene file whose InputSensor command buffer cascades prototype sub-graph deletion during gf_sg_vrml_parent_destroy, causing denial of service.

GPAC MP4Box before 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in the XMT parser that leaves parser->command_buffer pointing into a freed InputSensor node. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene file triggering a parse error so xmt_node_start() writes NULL into freed memory, corrupting the heap and crashing MP4Box.

Attendize through 2.8.0 contains a cross-account authorization bypass vulnerability in EventAttendeesController::postMessageAttendees() that allows authenticated organisers to message other accounts' attendees by supplying a foreign event_id. Attackers, including self-registered organisers, can post to the attendees message endpoint for another event to send arbitrary emails to all attendees, enabling phishing and impersonation.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in xmt_node_end() that allows attackers to corrupt memory by attaching nodes from unrelated proto sub-graphs to field-replace commands. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene buffering such a command in a Conditional node, causing gf_node_try_destroy() to access the freed node, crashing MP4Box and corrupting the heap.

GPAC MP4Box before 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in the XMT loader that allows attackers to crash the process by supplying crafted XMT files. Attackers can assign a second node to an SFNode command field so xmt_node_end() frees a forward-referenced child still cached in peeked_nodes, triggering a crash during DEF lookup in xmt_find_node().

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains an uncontrolled recursion vulnerability in gf_sg_proto_field_is_sftime_offset() in src/scenegraph/vrml_proto.c that allows attackers to crash MP4Box via crafted files. Attackers can supply an MP4 file whose BIFS scene contains cyclic PROTO IS relations, causing unbounded recursion that exhausts the stack and causes denial of service.

A flaw was found in gdm. The CreateRemoteDisplay D-Bus method fails to perform proper authorization checks when initiating a remote display session. A local attacker with access to the login screen environment can invoke this method with an arbitrary username to bypass standard automatic login verification checks. This vulnerability allows the attacker to achieve privilege escalation and start an unauthorized session as any user on the system, including root.
Rejected reason: This candidate is a duplicate of CVE-2026-132923. All CVE users should reference CVE-2026-132923 instead of this candidate.

FlowIntel contains an authorization flaw in its duplicate alert ingestion logic. When a duplicate alert is received and its content is updated, the ownership and visibility scope fields (owner user and owner organization) were not refreshed to reflect the connector's current scope. As a result, an alert that was originally created under a broader visibility scope retained that broader scope even after the connector's scope was narrowed or changed.

This means that users or organizations that should no longer have visibility into a given alert could continue to access it, because the stale ownership fields were never updated during the duplicate-update path. The issue affected all duplicate updates, including those involving alerts in terminal review states and those recovered from uniqueness conflicts.

Security impact:
- Unauthorized disclosure of security alert content to users or organizations outside the intended visibility scope.
- Stale access persists indefinitely until the alert is independently re-scoped or deleted.

Affected version: <4.1.0.

modified eCommerce Shopsoftware through 3.3.0 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability in gv_send.php because the action=process step never validates a CSRF token via check_secure_form(). Attackers can host an auto-submitting form that makes a logged-in customer send their gift voucher balance to an attacker-controlled email address for redemption.

Caddy – WooCommerce Side Cart & Free Shipping Bar plugin for WordPress 3.0.0 before 3.2.1 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the saved-items/add REST endpoint that exposes non-public product data. Authenticated attackers with Subscriber-level access can enumerate product_id values to read names, prices, images and stock status of private, draft, hidden and password-protected products.

Redmine 6.1.0 before 6.1.6 and 7.0.0 before 7.0.3 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that lets OAuth clients exceed token scope during project creation. A client with only project-creation scope can set is_public, enabled_module_names and inherit_members, making projects public and granting parent-project members subproject access.

Termix 1.7.0 before 26.11.2 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows authenticated users to write files outside the export directory via crafted usernames. Attackers can self-register with a username containing ../ segments and request POST /database/export to plant attacker-controlled SQLite files in writable directories, enabling disk exhaustion.

WebToffee Product Feed before 2.4.4 for WordPress contains a use of hard-coded cryptographic key vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to bypass the URL-cron signature check by computing a valid hash using the publicly known constant salt embedded in the plugin source. Attackers can send forged GET requests with attacker-controlled parameters to the unauthenticated init-hooked endpoint to repeatedly trigger product-feed generation, causing CPU/database resource exhaustion and overwriting of the generated feed file.

flowintel contains a CSV injection vulnerability in its audit log CSV export functionality. Attacker-influenced text recorded in audit logs could be interpreted as spreadsheet formulas when an administrator opened the exported CSV file in a spreadsheet application.

The vulnerable behavior allowed an attacker who could influence audit log content (for example by generating network traffic that is captured and logged) to embed formula-like strings (such as =CMD() or =HYPERLINK()) into audit entries. When the resulting CSV export was opened in a spreadsheet application, these strings could be executed as formulas, potentially leading to data exfiltration, data manipulation, or execution of further malicious actions within the spreadsheet context.

Preconditions:
- An attacker must be able to influence content that is recorded in flowintel audit logs.
- An administrator or user must export the audit logs to CSV and open the file in a spreadsheet application that interprets formulas.

Security impact:
- Potential information disclosure from the spreadsheet or linked resources.
- Potential integrity impact on data within the spreadsheet application.
- No direct compromise of the flowintel application itself.

Affected version: <4.1.0

### Summary ui

With `strip_ansi=True`, Pydantic AI Harness's `ToolOutputLimits` capability removes ANSI escape sequences from tool output with a pattern that takes time quadratic in the length of a line. A tool result of a few hundred kilobytes, crafted with many unterminated escape sequences, can occupy the event loop for tens of seconds to minutes, delaying every other request and agent run in the process.

### Details

This affects applications that set `strip_ansi=True` on `ToolOutputLimits` (named `OverflowingToolOutput` before 0.13.0) and run tools whose output an attacker can influence, such as shell commands, file reads, fetched pages or MCP servers. Stripping runs on the event loop before the capability reduces the output, so its own size limits do not bound it.

The assumed attacker can place text in content a tool returns.

### Mitigation

Upgrade `pydantic-ai-harness` to 0.70.0 or later. Until then, leave `strip_ansi` at its default, `False`.

On Pydantic AI v1, the harness cannot be upgraded past 0.4.0. Upgrade to Pydantic AI v2 and `pydantic-ai-harness` 0.70.0, or leave `strip_ansi` off.

MISP contains an authorization bypass affecting the event protection mechanism. In MISP, a protected event is designed to be modifiable only through the events/edit endpoint with a valid cryptographic signature. However, the protection check was enforced solely on that single route. All other write endpoints that operate on an event—attributes (add, edit, delete), objects (delete), events (populate, publish, unprotect, upload_sample, upload_analysis_file), tags (attach, detach), event reports (edit, delete), galaxy clusters (attach, detach), and cryptographic keys (add, delete)—lacked the equivalent check.

As a result, an authenticated user holding the sync permission (perm_sync) who is neither a site administrator nor an internal sync user (perm_sync_internal), and who belongs to the same organization as the event's creator (orgc_id), could modify, delete, or add data to a protected event without providing a valid signature. This included the ability to unprotect the event entirely, publish it to other instances, and add cryptographic signing keys that would subsequently permit signed edits, effectively nullifying the protection mechanism.

The vulnerability requires an authenticated sync user account within the event's creator organization. No user interaction or special network conditions are required; standard API calls to the affected endpoints are sufficient. The security impact is a loss of integrity over protected threat-intelligence events: an attacker can inject, alter, or remove attributes, objects, tags, reports, and galaxy cluster associations, and can remove the protection flag or add signing keys to enable persistent unauthorized modification.

MISP contains an authorization and scope flaw in the ObjectReference model's captureReference method. When a user saves an event (via REST API, sync, or feeds), any object reference included in the payload is looked up by its UUID across the entire MISP instance rather than being scoped to the event being saved. An authenticated user with permission to add or edit events can therefore include the UUID of an object reference belonging to a different event—including events in other organizations that the user cannot view—and cause the system to overwrite that foreign reference's relationship_type, comment, deleted flag, and timestamp with attacker-supplied values. The affected reference is neither deleted nor recreated in the attacker's event; its fields are silently rewritten in place. This constitutes a cross-tenant integrity violation: data integrity of object references in events the attacker has no read or write access to is compromised. The vulnerability is reachable through any event save path (REST add/edit, inter-instance sync, feed ingestion) and requires only a valid authenticated session with event modification privileges and knowledge or discovery of a target reference UUID.

OFFIS DCMTK 3.7.1 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in togglePlanarConfiguration8 and togglePlanarConfiguration16 in djcodece.cc, which compute row offsets using rows instead of columns. Attackers can supply a crafted color-by-plane DICOM image with more rows than columns that is compressed with the true-lossless JPEG codec to corrupt heap memory, causing crashes and potentially code execution.

Tiptap @tiptap/core 2.0.0-alpha.0 before 3.30.4 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows attackers to inject DOM attributes via a __proto__ key passed to mergeAttributes(). Attackers can supply untrusted JSON attribute data whose __proto__ replaces the merged object's prototype, causing DOMSerializer.renderSpec to render injected event handlers that execute JavaScript.

Cozy Cloud cozy-stack 1.6.62 before 1.6.69 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the shared-drive move handler that allows authenticated users to access other instances' files. Attackers owning a shared drive can name another instance's domain and any directory ID as the move source to copy and delete the victim's file tree.

HotGo 2.18.6 through 2.19.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated backend users to read other administrators' private letters because the messageIds helper omits the receiver filter. Low-privilege users can call GET /admin/notice/pullMessages, which is exempt from role permission checks via exceptAuth, to retrieve titles, contents and senders of private letters.

MISP contains an authorization bypass in its server-to-server proposal synchronization mechanism. Two related flaws were identified:

1. The events/pushProposals endpoint located the target event by UUID without enforcing any access-control check. A sync user with perm_sync could push shadow-attribute proposals to any event on the local instance, including events with restricted distribution (e.g., distribution level 0, visible only to the owning organisation). The stored proposal also carried the sender-supplied event_uuid and event_org_id rather than the local event's actual identity, corrupting the data model.

2. When accepting an edit proposal (old_id != 0), the code resolved the target live attribute by UUID alone (Attribute.uuid = shadow.uuid) without scoping the lookup to the proposal's own event. A malicious sync user could therefore craft a proposal whose uuid matched an attribute in a different event; upon acceptance, the wrong attribute would be modified or deleted. The same unscoped lookup existed in the ShadowAttribute::acceptProposal path.

Preconditions: an authenticated user with sync permission (perm_sync) on a MISP instance that participates in server-to-server synchronisation. The attacker must know or enumerate the UUID of a target event or attribute.

Security impact: unauthorised read access to restricted events, unauthorised insertion of proposals onto events the user cannot see, and unauthorised modification or deletion of attributes belonging to other events. This compromises the confidentiality and integrity of threat-intelligence data across organisational boundaries within a MISP deployment.

MISP contains an authorization flaw in the sharing group capture logic. When a sharing group is re-captured with a newer modified timestamp and an updated roster, the application unconditionally overwrote the type, nationality, sector, and contacts fields of every organisation listed in the roster, including the host organisation. This behaviour was reachable by any user holding the perm_sync role, and additionally by any external server pulled from or any feed fetched, because those operations execute with the privileges of the site administrator who initiated them. As a result, a low-privileged sync user or a malicious/compromised external feed or pull source could silently corrupt organisation records on the receiving MISP instance without any site-admin or internal-sync authorization. The vulnerability does not disclose data or affect availability; the impact is limited to integrity of organisation metadata (type, nationality, sector, contacts). The fix restricts organisation detail updates to internal sync operations (pulls over links flagged as internal, or senders holding perm_sync_internal) and site administrators; all other sync, pull, and feed operations may only match existing organisations by UUID or create new ones, without modifying their stored details.

flowintel allows users with editor-level access to author case and task fields, including aggregated tags. When these records are exported as CSV, the field values are written verbatim into the output file.

Because no sanitisation is applied to user-supplied text before CSV serialisation, an attacker can store values that begin with spreadsheet formula triggers (such as =, +, -, @, or their fullwidth Unicode equivalents, or leading control/whitespace characters). When a victim opens the exported CSV in a spreadsheet application (e.g. Microsoft Excel, LibreOffice Calc), the stored text is interpreted and executed as a live formula rather than displayed as literal text.

This can lead to unintended data manipulation within the spreadsheet, potential data exfiltration via formula functions, or execution of downstream commands depending on the spreadsheet application and its configuration.

The vulnerability requires the victim to actively open the CSV file in a spreadsheet application; the flowintel application itself is not directly compromised.

In JetBrains Rider before 2026.3 code execution was possible via MSBuild configuration files in parent directories
In JetBrains ReSharper before 2026.3 the What's New feature did not verify server certificates
In JetBrains ReSharper before 2026.3 server host names were not verified during certificate validation
In JetBrains IntelliJ IDEA before 2026.3 the GitHub plugin exposed GitHub access tokens via its public API

MISP contains an authorization flaw in the handling of remote pull and feed operations. When a non-internal pull or a feed processes incoming data and encounters an existing sharing group, the application did not verify that the remote server's organization was actually a member of that sharing group before allowing the group's metadata to be updated. The captureRemote mechanism previously stored only a boolean flag indicating whether the link was internal, and the authorization check in captureSGExisting relied solely on that flag. For non-internal pulls and feeds, the check was insufficient: a remote server whose organization was not a member of the target sharing group could still cause the group record to be modified (for example, altering the local flag, the modified timestamp, or other group properties). A feed, which has no associated server organization at all, could likewise trigger an update to an existing sharing group's metadata. The security impact is an integrity violation: an authenticated remote entity with sync or feed privileges can alter sharing group attributes that govern how data is distributed among organizations, potentially changing the local flag or other access-relevant properties of groups it does not belong to. The vulnerability requires an authenticated user with the ability to initiate a pull or feed (a sync user or feed administrator) and a target sharing group that exists on the local instance. No unauthenticated access or user interaction is required.

A command injection vulnerability was found in OpenStack Cinder's SSH-based storage-driver support. Incomplete validation of shell metacharacters allows an authenticated user who owns a volume on an affected backend to supply crafted connection information and inject additional commands into the storage array's management interface. Commands execute with the privileges of Cinder's configured backend account. This can disclose storage configuration information and, where that account has administrative permissions, could allow changes that affect the integrity or availability of other tenants' storage.

MISP, a threat intelligence sharing platform, contains a vulnerability in its cryptographic key management for protected (PGP-signed) events. Two related defects allow a revoked PGP key to remain effective for signing and validating protected events.

First, the validateProtectedEvent() method in the CryptographicKey model iterates over the event's stored cryptographic keys to verify a PGP signature but does not check the revoked flag on each key. A key explicitly marked as revoked is still used to validate signatures, meaning an entity whose key has been revoked can continue to sign protected events and have them accepted by the MISP instance.

Second, the captureCryptographicKeyUpdate() method, responsible for synchronizing the key list when a sync user edits a protected event, contained a query bug (find('first') instead of find('all')) that caused only the first stored key to be considered. As a result, revocations of additional keys were never persisted, keys absent from the pushed list were not removed, and entries lacking an explicit fingerprint were mismatched and incorrectly deleted. Additionally, the revocation logic did not enforce the invariant that a revocation, once stored, is never lifted by subsequent pushes.

A third minor issue: a signed protected event submitted without any cryptographic keys triggered an unhandled 500 error rather than a proper rejection response.

Preconditions: the attacker must be an authenticated sync user with permission to add or edit protected events on the MISP instance. The impact is that revoked keys retain signing authority, key revocations propagated by sync partners are silently dropped, and the integrity of the protected-event trust chain is compromised. In a multi-instance MISP deployment, events signed by revoked keys can propagate to other instances, extending the integrity impact across the sync network.
In JetBrains Junie GitHub Action before 1.10.0 untrusted fork code could be processed in privileged workflow runs
In JetBrains Junie GitHub Action before 1.10.0 code execution was possible via path traversal in feedback session markers
In JetBrains Junie GitHub Action before 1.10.0 command injection was possible via the action version input
In JetBrains Junie CLI before 26.11.1 files outside the project could be overwritten via shell output redirection
In JetBrains Junie CLI before 26.9.22 command injection was possible via file names in code review

A flaw was found in Keycloak. An authenticated remote user with a pending required security action, such as configuring multi-factor authentication (MFA), can bypass the mandatory action by submitting a specially crafted request to the consent endpoint without a valid session code. Keycloak incorrectly interprets the submission as a page refresh and completes the authentication process, allowing the user to access the application without fulfilling the required security policies.

Modoboa before 2.13.0 contains a CRLF injection vulnerability that allows Resellers or users with domain add or change permission to inject rspamd DKIM selector map entries by supplying an unvalidated dkim_key_selector through the relay domain API. Attackers can embed a carriage return in the selector to override another tenant's domain selector, causing rspamd to sign its outgoing mail with a nonexistent selector and fail DKIM verification.

OpnForm before 2.8.2 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in PublicWebhookUrl::isPublicIp that fails to reject CGNAT, NAT64 and 6to4 address ranges. Authenticated users can configure webhook, form import or PDF image URLs resolving to these ranges to make the server send HTTPS requests to internal hosts.

parse5-html-rewriting-stream 7.0.0 before 8.1.1 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability in RewritingStream#emitText, which skips escaping based on a stale lastStartTagName. Attackers can place entity-encoded markup after a closed script or style element to bypass RewritingStream-based filters and execute script in users' browsers.

modified eCommerce Shopsoftware through 3.3.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows administrators with product editing permission to inject script via the products_name field. The unescaped name is rendered in the h1 heading of product detail and reviews pages, executing script in the browsers of shoppers and logged-in customers.
In JetBrains IntelliJ IDEA before 2026.3, 2026.2.4 code execution was possible in untrusted projects via the Code Provenance plugin
In JetBrains YouTrack before 2026.2.19840 privilege escalation from project administrator to system administrator was possible via group merging
In JetBrains YouTrack before 2026.2.19840 an HTML injection in email notifications was possible via issue descriptions
In JetBrains YouTrack before 2026.2.19766 improper authorization allowed read-only users to change the visibility of restricted issues via agile boards
In JetBrains YouTrack before 2026.2.19840 the attachment upload size limit could be bypassed via the REST API
In JetBrains YouTrack before 2026.2.19840 project members could detach inline comment threads of other users on articles
In JetBrains YouTrack before 2026.2.19728 missing authorization allowed creating sub-articles without the Create Article permission

A vulnerability in the Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) component of Mitel MiCollab through 10.3 (10.3.0.18) could allow an unauthenticated attacker to leverage pre-staged malicious content to conduct an XML injection attack due to insufficient parameter validation. A successful exploit could allow an attacker to execute arbitrary commands within the context of the system. This is MTLVULN-1862.

ClassiCube before 1.4.0 contains a heap-based out-of-bounds write vulnerability in Png_Decode in src/Bitmap.c that allows malicious servers to corrupt client memory by sending a PNG with a duplicate IHDR chunk. Attackers can supply crafted PNGs via texture pack URLs or player skins so the unreset bufferIdx underflows remaining space, letting IDAT data overflow the buffer to crash clients or execute code.

A vulnerability in the Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) component of Mitel MiCollab through 10.3 (10.3.0.18) could allow an unauthenticated attacker, with knowledge of a specific system-generated random identifier or pre-staged content, to conduct an unauthorized access attack due to improper authentication mechanisms. A successful exploit could allow an attacker to obtain sensitive information. The vulnerability is limited to the affected functionality and does not provide unrestricted access to arbitrary files elsewhere on the system. This is MTLVULN-1863.

A vulnerability in the Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) component of Mitel MiCollab through 10.3 (10.3.0.18) could allow an unauthenticated attacker to conduct a blind command injection attack due to insufficient parameter sanitization. A successful exploit could allow an attacker to execute arbitrary commands within the context of the system. This is MTLVULN-1864.

A flaw was found in KServe. A namespace-scoped user with create/update permissions on InferenceService custom resources can exploit this vulnerability by providing a malicious `storageUri`. This Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability allows the `storage-initializer` init container to issue arbitrary outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests from inside the cluster. This can lead to information disclosure, including credential theft for the node's Identity and Access Management (IAM) role or access to internal cluster services.

The WP Duplicate – WordPress Migration Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Remote Code Execution in all versions up to, and including, 1.1.11 via the save_single_batch_file function. This is due to a PHP type-juggling authentication bypass via loose != comparison with no is_string() guard, combined with unsanitized base64-decoded path construction in save_single_batch_file() lacking any directory traversal containment. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with custom-level access and above, to execute code on the server. Exploitation requires that the site owner has completed the plugin's initial setup so that the site_type and prod_key_random_id options are non-empty, though any non-empty secret value is bypassable via the type-juggling flaw.

A server-side request forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in the Pure Storage FlashArray extension for Windows Admin Center versions could allow an authenticated Gateway User to direct the management gateway to an unintended host, potentially exposing stored FlashArray credentials and API tokens and allowing unauthorized access to the managed FlashArray.

Mattermost versions 11.11.x <= 11.11.0, 11.7.x <= 11.7.11, 11.10.x <= 11.10.2 fail to bound the resources consumed while processing an uploaded custom emoji image which allows an authenticated user with default permissions to make the server unresponsive for all users via repeated custom emoji uploads.. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00720

Mattermost versions 11.7.x <= 11.7.11 fail to sanitize channel mentions when rendering permalinked posts, which allows an authenticated user to discover the display names of private channels they do not have access to via a permalink to a post that mentions the channel.. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00721

A flaw was found in librest. The PKCE implementation for OAuth authorization uses the GRand function from the GLib API, a cryptographically insecure pseudo-random number generator. Because the generated "code verifier" lacks sufficient cryptographic entropy, a malicious actor can reverse-engineer the pseudo-random number generator (PRNG) seed to predict or reconstruct the code verifier string, allowing an attacker to bypass PKCE protections and successfully impersonate the client during the OAuth 2.0 authorization flow.
IBM API Connect 10.0.8.0 through 10.0.8.12 and 12.1.0.0 through 12.1.1.2 could allow a remote authenticated attacker to gain elevated privileges due to improper authentication.

IBM API Connect 12.1.0.0 through 12.1.1.2 could allow a remote authenticated attacker to falsify audit log information due to reliance on untrusted inputs. Information supplied by the client is relied on when recording the source of a request, so audit records could contain inaccurate details.

IBM API Connect 10.0.8.0 through 10.0.8.12 and 12.1.0.0 through 12.1.1.2 could allow a remote authenticated attacker to bypass security restrictions due to improper authentication. Information supplied by the client is not sufficiently verified, which could allow a caller to impersonate another party.
IBM API Connect 12.1.0.0 through 12.1.1.2 could allow a remote authenticated attacker to obtain sensitive information due to improper validation of user-supplied URLs.
IBM API Connect 10.0.8.0 through 10.0.8.12 and 12.1.0.0 through 12.1.1.2 could allow a remote attacker to bypass security restrictions due to LDAP injection.

IBM API Connect 12.1.0.0 through 12.1.1.2 could allow a remote authenticated attacker to obtain sensitive information due to server-side request forgery. Destination restrictions on outbound requests can be bypassed, which could allow the server to retrieve content from unintended resources.
IBM API Connect 10.0.8.0 through 10.0.8.12 and 12.1.0.0 through 12.1.1.2 could allow a remote authenticated attacker to obtain sensitive information due to broken object-level authorization.
IBM API Connect 12.1.0.0 through 12.1.1.2 could allow a remote authenticated attacker to access internal resources and cause a denial of service due to server-side request forgery.
IBM API Connect 10.0.8.0 through 10.0.8.12 and 12.1.0.0 through 12.1.1.2 could allow a remote authenticated attacker to obtain sensitive information due to improper authorization.

IBM API Connect 12.1.0.0 through 12.1.1.2 could allow a remote authenticated attacker to obtain sensitive information due to improper input validation. Input checks are incomplete, which could allow them to be bypassed.

Mattermost versions 11.11.x <= 11.11.0, 11.7.x <= 11.7.11, 11.10.x <= 11.10.2 fail to enforce the channel Access Control Policy's file download permission check when serving file metadata and thumbnails through the drafts, scheduled posts, and post edit history endpoints, which allows an authenticated user who has lost eligibility under the policy to view metadata and thumbnails of file attachments via those endpoints, even though direct file access is correctly denied. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00740

Editor to make a board or card permanently unopenable for all users via a crafted PATCH
request storing a non-string property name or value.. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00743

Mattermost versions 11.11.x <= 11.11.0, 11.7.x <= 11.7.11, 11.10.x <= 11.10.2 fail to enforce the MFA requirement on the update and delete user endpoints, which allows an authenticated user who has not configured MFA to modify or delete their own account via the API despite system-wide MFA enforcement being enabled. Mattermost versions 11.7.x <= 11.7.11, 11.10.x <= 11.10.2, 11.11.x <= 11.11.1 fail to enforce the configured GitLab group/namespace restriction on the permalink code-preview feature and the {{get_projects}} MCP tool, which allows an authenticated user with a connected GitLab account to retrieve repository file content or project metadata from projects outside the restricted group via a crafted GitLab permalink or MCP tool call. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00750

Mattermost versions 11.7.x <= 11.7.11 fail to scope an incoming webhook's direct message target to the webhook's own team, which allows a team administrator to deliver a direct message to a user on a team they have no authority over via a webhook whose posting identity belongs to both teams..
